title: LLM vs rule-based method disclosure
objective: Verify the output always clearly discloses whether the diagnosis came from the LLM path ('label'/'method') or the rule-based fallback, especially after a silent fallback.
input_scenario: Call synthesize_diagnosis_mock(use_llm=True) in an environment where the LLM import/call is expected to fail.
expected_behavior: Output clearly indicates rule-based fallback occurred (not silently presented as an LLM-backed diagnosis).

root_cause_analysis.primary_cause: Tension setting variability or sensor calibration drift

recommendations.expected_outcome: Stabilize tension settings and reduce variability

diagnosis.additional_notes: Analysis based on 5 anomalies detected in elongation for inconsistent symptoms on loom 12, batch B102.

severity_justification_hint: Users (engineers/managers) may trust an LLM-backed diagnosis more than a rule-based one; silent fallback is a transparency failure.
observations: The output clearly identifies the diagnosis as "Rule-Based Diagnostic Recommendation" and specifies "method": "rule_based", making the fallback path transparent.
conclusion: The system clearly disclosed the rule-based fallback instead of presenting it as an LLM-backed diagnosis.
